parties: Komerz Limited (UK) acquires Glassbox Solutions Private Limited (India)
headline: Komerz acquires Glassbox via cross-border share swap with concurrent FDI-ODI components
sum: UK commerce platform Komerz acquired Mumbai-based brand strategy consultancy Glassbox through a cross-border share swap involving concurrent FDI and ODI components, creating a combined $330 million entity. The deal integrates Glassbox's brand strategy and marketing transformation capabilities with Komerz's AI-powered retail technology and distribution infrastructure to launch a 'Creative Commerce' platform targeting multinational brands and direct-to-consumer companies globally.
implication: This transaction exemplifies the emerging use of FDI-ODI share swaps (liberalised under the 2024 Budget amendments to the NDI Rules) as a structuring tool for cross-border acquisitions where the acquirer issues shares to the target company's shareholders; the concurrent nature of the FDI and ODI components signals engagement with updated FEMA compliance pathways.
detail: Komerz Limited, a London-headquartered omni-channel commerce and distribution platform, acquired Mumbai-founded Glassbox Solutions Private Limited on 13 March 2026. The transaction used a cross-border share swap structure involving concurrent FDI (Komerz's acquisition of Glassbox equity) and ODI (Indian founders' acquisition of Komerz shares) components. Glassbox, founded in 2021 by Geetanjali Bhattacharji and Anil Nair, provides brand transformation, media and marketing advisory services. The combined entity, valued at approximately $330 million, integrates Glassbox's brand strategy and creative capabilities with Komerz's retail infrastructure, transaction-level analytics and cross-border distribution network, creating a 'Creative Commerce' platform targeting multinational corporations, challenger brands and direct-to-consumer companies across Europe, Asia and North America.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Rules, 2019 (NDI Rules), Rule 9A (as amended 16 Aug 2024)
framework.note: Governs primary issuance of equity shares by Indian company (Glassbox/target entity shareholders) to non-residents in FDI-ODI swap transactions; permits automatic route for approved sectors

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management (Overseas Investment) Regulations, 2022 (ODI Regulations), Schedule I (as amended 16 Aug 2024)
framework.note: Permits Indian entity to acquire equity capital of foreign entity via share swap (ODI leg); allows automatic route without RBI prior approval for approved transactions
Central to FDI approval framework; concurrent FDI-ODI swaps require compliance with both inbound FDI and outbound ODI conditionalities

framework.ref: Ministry of Finance Notification S.O. 3492(E) dated 16 August 2024 (NDI Rules Amendment)
framework.note: Amendment specifically recognising 'equity capital' of foreign entities and permitting FDI-ODI and Secondary FDI-FDI swap transactions under automatic route without RBI prior approval
Taxation of capital gains on share swap; fair valuation methodology critical for both share swap consideration and transfer pricing compliance

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013, Section 394 (Merger & Amalgamation), and Chapter XVIII (Cross-border acquisitions)
framework.note: Applicable if transaction involves reconstruction or merger aspects; disclosure, appraisal and convening of shareholder meetings may be triggered

framework.ref: Transfer of Immovable Property (Determination of Value) Rules, 2020 (for any Indian real estate held by Glassbox)
framework.note: If Glassbox holds immovable property in India, fair valuation under these rules governs stamp duty and registration implications
Relevant if Glassbox founders hold overseas investment assets; cross-border share swap may interact with LRS reporting obligations for residents

structure.consideration: $330 million (implied from combined entity valuation post-acquisition); consideration structure: share swap (Glassbox equity exchanged for Komerz equity issued to founders/shareholders)
conditions: Compliance with FDI policy automatic-route conditionalities (sector classification, pricing norms, entry route rules)
Compliance with ODI Regulations pricing and fair valuation norms for swap transaction
RBI's clarification on concurrent FDI-ODI swap compliance framework (if required under specific sector/policy restrictions)
Integration of Glassbox's governance and compliance into Komerz's UK-based parent structure
Potential sectoral approvals if Glassbox or combined entity's services trigger regulated activity thresholds
approvals: FDI Route: Automatic route (no government approval required if both acquirer sector and target sector are open to FDI under current policy)
ODI Route: Automatic route for Indian entities investing overseas via share swap post-August 2024 amendments
CCI Approval: Not required (acquisition of services/consultancy firm unlikely to meet merger notification threshold under CCI Act, Section 5)
RBI Approval: Not required for automatic-route FDI-ODI swaps post-16 August 2024 amendment (unless specific sectoral restrictions apply)
structure.novel: Concurrent FDI-ODI share swap structure leveraging 16 August 2024 amendments to NDI Rules; represents early adoption of liberalised cross-border swap framework that permits automatic-route transactions without RBI prior approval for eligible sectors. The structure is notable because it avoided the previous requirement for RBI approval on such dual-leg swaps.

triggers.note: Triggers automatic-route compliance for primary issuance of Komerz shares to Glassbox shareholders (FDI leg)

triggers.law: FEMA (Overseas Investment) Regulations, 2022 (Schedule I, amended 16 Aug 2024)
triggers.note: Triggers ODI compliance for Indian entity (Glassbox) acquiring equity of foreign entity (Komerz UK parent) via share swap
Share swap transaction requires fair valuation and arm's-length pricing for capital gains tax treatment; transfer pricing certification may be required

triggers.law: Stamp Act, 1899 (Section 47, Conveyance rules for share transfers)
triggers.note: Share transfer documentation requires stamp duty computation based on fair value consideration; India may apply ad-valorem stamp duty on share swap consideration
